findings.summary: Empty-board auto-seeding is absent from the entry, so spec §1.1 (carry over E0a's 空板自播种) and acceptance criterion 5 (auto-seeding effective and idempotent, repeated runs do not double board clues) are unmet. bin/e0-regression.sh only ensures the four channels then runs the loop; nothing publishes research.clue.v2 seed clues (the existing tick-entry --seed / runSeed path is never invoked outside tests, and no test covers criterion 5). On a freshly created empty TICK_CHANNEL the loop has no cards, emits no CAS writes and no continuation, so head_seq cannot grow and Z1 (criterion 8) is unreachable by construction — the same 'entry can never reach a passing Z1' shape that got E0a rejected.

The terminal-state assertion was dropped instead of being converted to real JSON parsing. Spec §1.2 requires that extracting termination.state from the loop output also use a real JSON parse ('bin/e0-regression.sh 里现有三处 sed -n 抽取都要按此改'), criterion 4 requires a non-zero exit when the loop exits 0 but the board has no terminal state, and §3 explicitly forbids relaxing the terminal-state assertion to '没报错就算过'. The entry now derives FINAL_EXIT solely from LOOP_EXIT plus bin/e0-verify.sh, which only compares head_seq/sum; run.stdout.log is archived but never parsed, and neither bin/e0-regression.sh nor bin/e0-verify.sh mentions termination at all. A run that writes clues yet ends with termination.state === null (hasPendingWork false but zeroGrowthRounds below threshold) exits 0 and passes.

The loud-failure message does not name the actual field set as §1.1 requires. parseChannelList collapses each list entry to head_seq|null, so the per-channel field set is discarded; snapshot() then prints Object.keys(channels), i.e. the list of channel_ids, labelled 'actual field set'. In the 'channel present but head_seq missing' case the operator gets channel names instead of the fields actually returned — exactly the diagnostic that made the E0a real-machine failure hard to attribute.

The fake bus still diverges from the real agent-bus for list membership: GET /v1/channels iterates only channels that already hold messages and there is no POST /v1/channels handler, so a created-but-empty channel (which the real bus lists with head_seq 0) is absent from the fixture's list response. Combined with the fact that no test drives the e0-metrics CLI over HTTP against the fixture (only the pure functions and the field-set contract are tested), the 'created channel then read its head_seq' path the entry actually depends on remains unexercised.

bin/e0-verify.sh emits the Z1 failure text 'loop wrote nothing or board has no terminal state' although it only checks head_seq growth; the message overstates what was verified and would mislead triage on a run that wrote to the bus without reaching a terminal state.
